For a laptop screen extender that works without installing drivers, I'd prioritize models that use native USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode or HDMI.

The key distinction is that some screen extenders advertise "single-cable USB-C" but actually require DisplayLink or proprietary software. Those are not truly driver-free.

My recommendation: Look for a dual-screen extender with native video input, or a portable monitor from ASUS or Lenovo if reliability matters more than having two extra screens.

Here are the options I'd consider.

Best driver-free options

1. UPERFECT - 14" Dual Laptop Screen Extender - 1080P IPS Porta…

Best value — dual screen

Two 14-inch 1080p screens, USB-C/HDMI, clip-on design. Advertised as driver-free. 
Best Buy

$139.99

2. INVZI - MagHub Dual 15.6" Laptop Screen Extender, Triple Scr…

Two 15.6-inch Full HD screens. Driver-free USB-C and Mini HDMI connectivity; larger workspace but bulkier.

$319.00

3. ASUS ZenScreen MB16ACV

One standalone 15.6-inch screen. Native USB-C video works without extra drivers; USB-A mode requires a driver.

$194.99

For two larger displays, also consider the FOPO S11. It offers two 16-inch 1920 × 1200 panels and explicitly documents driver-free connections. 
FOPO

One important compatibility warning

A driver-free extender cannot bypass your laptop's native external-display limit. For example, some base M-series MacBooks cannot drive two independent external displays, even when the extender itself needs no drivers.
